Use `snl macro rename` to change one Macro identity while preserving complete structured-reference closure.

### Availability
This Entry is a normative product contract. The command is available exactly when machine-readable `snl --help` advertises `macro/rename`.

### Canonical command and request
The noun-first shell form is `snl macro rename <old-id> --to <new-id> --if-match <revision> [--dry-run] [--json] [--root <workspace>]`; its transport-neutral command is `macro/rename`. The exact source revision returned by `snl macro get` is mandatory for both dry-run and apply. Unknown flags/arguments, missing `--to`, or missing `--if-match` are invocation failures. `--dry-run` is the supported check/plan mode: it performs every read, parse, collision, reference-closure, and projected-validity check and returns the deterministic plan without writing.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"macro/rename","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{"id":"<exact-id>","to":"<new-id>","expectedRevision":"<opaque>","dryRun":false}}
```
Unknown argument keys are rejected by every adapter.

### Identity and closure
The destination must be non-empty, distinct, schema-valid, and, whenever it occurs in SNL, accepted as one complete identifier by the installed SNL-Basics authority parser. Do not apply an ASCII-only approximation. In particular the Macro destination `文法.之` is valid when the parser accepts it. The operation discovers the one source definition and every schema-owned occurrence, including SNL Macro references, Library-owned indexes when present, Macro-source-owned fields when present, Package-owned membership/index data when present, Relationship-owned fields when present, and generated witness metadata. It rewrites only occurrences owned by that identity: an unresolved fvar/bvar with the same spelling is not rewritten merely by textual equality. Canonical definition filenames and package membership/index ordering are recomputed. A missing or ambiguous definition, destination collision, dangling/unsupported occurrence, malformed SNL, or invalid projected workspace is rejected before publication.

### Concurrency and atomicity
The implementation acquires the shared workspace-data lock, verifies `--if-match` against the current source definition, rederives the complete plan under that lock, and rejects stale CAS or any intervening source drift. Apply publishes the definition and all owned references/indexes as one guarded transaction. Any install or post-write verification failure restores every already-installed source; success leaves no old identity, exactly one new definition, no dangling reference, and a valid workspace.

### Stable result and exit behavior
Under `--json`, stdout is exactly one newline-terminated `snl.result/v1` document. Success exits 0 with `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"macro/rename","data":{},"diagnostics":[]}`; `data` includes `dryRun`, `entityType`, `oldId`, `newId`, categorized `occurrences`, `changedFiles`, source revisions/planned outputs, and a deterministic plan fingerprint. Apply additionally includes canonical renamed-entity readback. Domain failures (not found, collision, stale revision/plan, invalid data or projected workspace) exit 1 with a stable error code and no write. Bad invocation, unsupported schema, input/runtime/lock failure exits 2. Failure JSON is `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"macro/rename","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","retryable":false}}`; stdout contains no prose or stack trace.
